caption.text:
Let’s be clear: Pride was never just about rainbows, parades, or corporate logos. It has always been about people. It has always been about protecting the right of every person to exist safely, openly, and freely.

At a time when LGBTQIA+ people, especially trans people, are facing increasing attacks on their rights, healthcare, visibility, and dignity, Pride remains as necessary as ever. Not because progress hasn’t been made, but because progress is fragile.

The rights we celebrate today are the result of people who organized, protested, resisted, and refused to disappear. And our responsibility is to ensure the next generation inherits more freedom, not less.

This page was built by a Black queer kid from the South who was once told people like him shouldn’t exist. The words you read here, the community built here, and the life lessons shared here are shaped by that lived experience.

So Happy Pride Month to everyone who has also experienced being told they were too much, not enough, or unworthy of belonging. You’ll always have a home here in this community. 

You deserve to be here. You always have. 🫶🏽 

✨ Featured artist to follow (slides 1-6): @sterlinggraves ✨

caption.text:
Some days it feels like the world asks far too much of the human heart.

A lot of people are emotionally exhausted right now. Not just from personal struggles, but from constantly witnessing cruelty, division, instability, and the erosion of basic humanity in real time. That kind of overwhelm changes the nervous system. It changes the body. It changes how safe the future feels.

Please be gentle with yourself.

Protect your peace, but not at the cost of your humanity. Rest when you need to. Log off when you need to. Feel what you need to feel. But do not let this world convince you that tenderness, compassion, truth, community, or hope are meaningless. Don’t let it strip you of the things that make you human. They still matter deeply.

There are still people trying. There are still people choosing love. There are still people resisting cruelty. There are still people protecting each other. People just like you.

And that matters too. 🧡

Written by @williegreene_

caption.text:
Leave a ❤️ below if this spoke to you. 

We lie to ourselves when we say we’re failing at life, when we shame ourselves for being “behind.” In reality, we are responding in a normal way to an increasingly exhausting world. One our nervous systems were not designed to naturally thrive in. 

I think a lot of us are carrying more than we even realize right now. Financial pressure. Constant stimulation. Grief. Fear. Isolation. Burnout. Uncertainty about the future. And somehow, we are still expected to function like everything is normal.

So if you’ve been feeling emotionally tired lately, let this be your reminder that your humanity is not a flaw.

Take care of yourself. Choose yourself, and your community. Stay informed. Stay soft. Stay awake. We need each other more than ever. We really do.

Written by @williegreene_

caption.text:
Sometimes choosing what’s right for your peace feels like punishment. It can feel heavy. Lonely. Even wrong. Especially when it’s tied to people you care about. But you have to remind yourself why you chose distance, why you stopped explaining, why you let go. If something or someone brings more chaos than calm, more self-doubt than self-worth, what are you really holding on to?⁠
⁠
Community is supposed to feel like safety. Like home. If you have to shrink to stay, if you’re constantly second-guessing your worth just to be accepted, then that’s not love. That’s survival. And you deserve more than just making yourself tolerable to people who can’t hold space for your fullness. That’s not living. That’s erasing yourself.

caption.text:
I don’t often share the real stories behind my life — I’ve always preferred the quiet corners, the pseudo-privacy that lets the work speak louder than I do. But something happened recently in the Great Bear Rainforest that I haven’t been able to shake.

I’d been searching for the elusive coastal wolves for years. They’re shy, careful, almost sacred creatures — the kind you don’t find unless they decide to let you. One morning, while kayaking upriver, I got stuck on a shallow patch of rocks. It forced me into stillness, the kind you don’t choose but somehow need. And in that suspended moment, they appeared.

One wolf stepped out of the trees. Then another. Then an entire pack. They could have vanished as quickly as they came, but instead they moved toward me — curious, cautious, impossibly close. For a few unforgettable minutes, I just existed there with them, breathing the same air, feeling the weight of their presence and their trust. It was one of the most surreal, spiritual encounters of my life. A reminder of how fragile the wild has become, and how much these creatures need us to protect what remains of their world.

I wrote the full story on Substack — the encounter, what it taught me, and how you can help protect wolves in British Columbia.
 It’s called A Moment With Wolves, and it might be the most personal thing I’ve shared. Check it out at the link in bio. 

Love from the shadows, Atticus

caption.text:
It’s strange how some things disappear without really announcing themselves.

One day you’re calling someone’s house phone, waiting for their mom to yell their name from another room, and it feels completely normal. One day you’re half-asleep in the backseat of the car, trusting that someone will carry you inside. One day the mall feels huge, Friday night TV feels important, and the streetlights coming on means the day is almost over.

And then years pass.

You don’t always miss the exact thing. You don’t necessarily want to go back to the phone, or the CD, or the computer screen, or the same old streets.

Sometimes you just miss the version of life where those little things still felt big.

Where you didn’t know you were inside a memory yet.

caption.text:
You are not behind in life. You are not late. You are not missing some secret timeline everyone else seems to understand. You are simply becoming.

The truth is, some of the most important transformations happen quietly. They happen in the moments nobody celebrates. In the boundaries you finally set. In the people you finally stop chasing. In the peace you choose over proving yourself. In the way you keep showing up for your life, even when you have no guarantee that things will work out.

Maybe this season hasn’t looked the way you hoped it would. Maybe there are still prayers unanswered, plans unfinished, and dreams that feel farther away than they did at the beginning of the year. But growth isn’t only found in arrival. Sometimes growth is found in the waiting. Sometimes it is found in trusting that what is meant for you is still finding its way to you.

One day, you’ll look back at this version of yourself with so much tenderness. You’ll realize that while you were worrying about how far you still had to go, you were already becoming the person you prayed to be.

If you needed a reminder today: the best chapters of your story do not belong to your past. They belong to your future.

Inspired by the book ‘Stay Single’ by Rebecca Simon — a book about choosing yourself, trusting your timing, and building a life so full that love becomes an addition to it, not a rescue from it 🖤

caption.text:
“Pre-order ‘How To Stop Breaking Your Own Heart’ now — out June 24, 2024.
—
What does a better you look like?

I remember being asked this question in therapy, and honestly, it didn’t take me long to respond. It’s easy to envision the perfect version of ourselves, a reality in which we live in freedom, beyond the constraints of what we subject ourselves to daily. I listed a bunch of things I would implement into my days to make them feel more fulfilled and productive, including all the qualities I would possess in order to have the ability to achieve these things.

My therapist responded with questions about my value system and my commitments to myself; it quickly became apparent that I wasn’t operating at my best, or even enough, to put these things into practice and bring them into my actual reality.

So, what was the issue? My foundations. I was still operating from a place of lack, from a mindset where I struggled to believe in myself or acknowledge my value. We have been led to believe that imposter syndrome is an individual issue, that only weak-minded people experience, when in fact, each and every one of us struggles with it. The only difference is, some people acknowledge what’s being said internally and choose to push past it, while others unfortunately allow themselves to get sucked into the lies and succumb.

My therapist made a point. He told me, “Your foundations are your grounds, your earth, your mud, your beginning. How can you expect anything to flourish in bad soil? Our foundations have to be set at a standard before anything has the chance to grow. We need to focus on developing your soil first and worry about planting seeds later.”

In my book, I talk about my journey to returning home to myself, the ways in which I had to break cycles, and the routes I took to find my way back.

Thank you in advance to everyone who has supported my work and placed an order.

It’s currently available for pre-order worldwide.
Published by @hayhouseuk

caption.text:
By now, I’m convinced that your soul knows when a season is coming to an end.

I never thought I’d be starting over at 36.

Grief, sadness, and depression held me for 1,706 days.

Stagnation. Procrastination. Complete hibernation from the version of me I once knew.

And yet, in the midst of all of that, my life’s work still stayed at the centre of my mind; every morning and every night.

I poured my soul into 2025, and with intention, I did everything needed to reclaim my life.

I survived the lowest of lows, and to be honest, rock bottom was the most freedom I’ve ever experienced.

There’s no urgency, almost everyone has written you off, and essentially, it’s just you vs. you.

The silence is loud. You’re faced with the reality of who you’ve become, and all you have is time, time to fix it.

Through all of these experiences, I’ve gained a deeper insight into life and collected so much wisdom.

I am of service, and I have so much to share. My spirit feels 100 years old.

I spoke to my elder Millie last night. We’re both Scorpios. She’s turning 93 next week.

She laughed when I told her that I feel like my life is over and reminded me that she has 56 years on me.

She said, “Starting over is just an invitation to return to the root of who you’ve become.”

It’s nothing to be ashamed of. If anything, it’s the complete opposite. What a privilege it is to be able to start over.

We’ve been led to believe that starting over is synonymous with failure,
 and because of that, many of us carry such deep levels of shame that we’d rather stay in positions we’ve outgrown than embrace the vulnerability of rebuilding something new.

So yeah, chipped nails, dry lips still showing up.

To anyone reading this: life can be rebuilt after loss, after trauma, after convincing ourselves that we aren’t worthy of experiencing it to its fullest extent.

Even if we’ve strayed light-years away from where we’re meant to be, we still have the ability to return home to ourselves.

🌻

caption.text:
My mother’s last wishes were for me to care for her father, my grandfather, and to ensure he wasn’t alone when it was time for him to transition.

The villain of the family. The man I wrote about in the opening chapter of my book, “How to Stop Breaking Your Own Heart,” and later, where I share a story about forgiveness and my mother’s journey to reconnecting with her father. My first heartbreak. The source of pain for my family for over 60 years.

A request I never understood, but knowing my mum, she had her reasons. So, I continued to trust her judgment in the three years since she passed away and cared for my grandfather.

This weekend, I buried my grandfather, closed a chapter, and broke a generational curse. Amidst all of this, I realized my mother’s last lesson for me was to understand and experience, for myself, the importance of forgiveness.

During this three-year process, I had no choice but to put my mental health first, regardless of who that offended. Many advised me to walk away and abandon my mother’s last request, underestimating that I live by a code and that my loyalty stretches far beyond the grave for those I cherish.

Some say I’m stubborn because I cannot be bought, persuaded, or controlled. But I know deep down, if I’ve been called to do something, then I will honor that and move accordingly until it is done.

In my book, I spoke about my mum reclaiming her life at the age of 60. I managed to do it by 34. My children will never have to walk this path.

This is what breaking generational curses looks like, and who feels it knows it.

Thank you to everyone who was patient with me during these years. I’ve been operating at 10% of my potential for over a decade and still managed to build a community of 24 million people and become a Sunday Times Best Selling Author. I’m excited to see how life changes now that I can pour 100% of my energy back into myself — in honour of my Mum and the years she lost.

Give thanks for freedom. 🙂

I pray, that if my Grandfathers soul has the opportunity to experience this life again, I hope he chooses to live in peace instead of pain. He deserves to know what that feels like too.

🌻

#breakinggenerationalcurses

caption.text:
Hi, my name is Atticus. You may not know me or maybe you do. It doesn’t really matter, but I’d like to tell a story. ⁠
⁠
It starts a few years ago when someone I knew died in a hotel room in Vancouver. Every time I saw him, I felt the same thing. The strange confusion of fame and sadness that I saw in so many famous people I knew. Fame is a tricky thing. On one hand, it gives you everything you want in life. On the other, it takes away everything you need. ⁠
⁠
That summer I took a trip to France, and through a friend, I met a guy named Michael Madsen. He’s the bad guy from Kill Bill, Reservoir Dogs, and a Justin Bieber music video. We became friends, and he taught me a lot about fame, about sadness, and how poetry had saved his life. How interesting. Here was a motorcycle-riding, whiskey-drinking American badass, telling me to write poetry. ⁠
⁠
A few days later, walking the streets of Paris, I saw something beautiful and wrote it down. I posted it online under the name, Atticus. Why? Because I liked the name. Not long after, I was offered my first book deal. And my publisher said --- you should take off the mask, you’ll sell a million books. But, all I could think of was why? For who? And at what cost? So, I kept the mask on. And I asked my fans who knew to help keep me hidden. They got it. They saw it for what it was, a guy who wanted to create things, but also, not be famous. ⁠
⁠
I realized that’s what Atticus is, it's not me at all, it’s all of you. And because I have no face, we put the face we need on the words, and Atticus becomes whoever we need. Because it’s not about who Atticus is. It’s about who you are. A woman once stood up at the end of one of my shows. I was wearing my mask. She said, in a world obsessed with fame, I think it’s beautiful you’re here--- sending love from the shadows. Love from the shadows, Atticus.⁠
⁠
xx Atticus⁠

You don’t have to have everything figured out right now.

You don’t need a five-year plan. You don’t need to suddenly become a different person overnight. You don’t need to prove that you’re making perfect use of every day.

You’ve already made it through things you once thought would break you. There are versions of you from the past that would be relieved to know you made it this far.

I know it’s easy to look around and feel behind. To wonder if everyone else understands something you somehow missed. To think you should be doing more, becoming more, fixing more.

But maybe you’re allowed to be a work in progress without treating yourself like a problem.

Maybe your life isn’t late.

Maybe you’re just living through a chapter that doesn’t make much sense while you’re inside it.

You are still growing, even on the days that feel ordinary. You are still changing, even when it seems like nothing is happening. And you are allowed to trust that not every good thing has already happened.

There are conversations you haven’t had yet that will stay with you for years. There are people you haven’t met yet who will be grateful you came into their lives. There are moments waiting for you that would make all this worrying feel strangely distant.

You don’t have to force your future into existence.

Just keep showing up.

Keep being curious.

Keep giving yourself the same patience you would give someone you love.

You might be a lot closer to the life you’re hoping for than you realize. ✨

caption.text:
✨Introduction✨

Welcome to my little corner on the internet. My name is Ron and this is my story. 

I left behind my life back home in 2017. Nothing was fundamentally wrong. But I was unhappy and I wanted my life to be more. I didn’t know what “more” meant, but I knew I wasn’t going to find it back home. So I had to leave. 

I skipped university and “the system” and made up my own path instead. 

At that time, everyone I knew wanted to travel but they also wanted to be “sensible”. I wanted both. I wanted to travel and experience life, but I also wanted to build a business and be more successful than everyone else while I travel. 

I didn’t know where to begin, but I knew what I needed was more exposure in order to figure it out. I saved up a bunch of money for university, and decided to use it to travel instead. 

I worked on my business and traveled full time at the same time. For the first 2 years, I mostly backpacked. I’ve worked backpacking jobs, I’ve worked for free in exchange for accommodation, I’d meet people on the road and travel with them together, and I’d work on my phone on the bunk bed of hostels. 

Everything was terribly chaotic and confusing. But I wasn’t unhappy anymore. Intuitively, I knew I was on the right path. I just had to keep going through it and I knew things would make sense eventually. 

Fast forward, it’s been almost 7 years. I started when I was 22. I am on my last year of twenties now. 

For the most part, I am still on the same path. I still want exposure to life, and I am still highly ambitious. I am not where I want to be yet, but I am no longer confused like I was in my early twenties.

I know what I want now. And I know that the “gap” between where I am and where I want to be is simply dedicated efforts in the right direction. I’m confident enough to know that if I keep trying, I will figure it out. 

Ultimately, what I want is simply a life I feel happy living in. Do things I love doing. Be with people I like being with.

My Instagram account is really just me trying to document my life as it happens. Live life and write about it. The good, the bad, the lessons learned, and the reflections. That’s all I’m trying to do here.

caption.text:
Missing them will try to convince you that you made a mistake. That maybe you should go back, that maybe you let go too soon, that maybe it could still work if you just tried one more time. But missing someone is not the same thing as being meant to be with them. It just means what you felt was real. 

It means there was love there, connection, something that mattered enough to leave an imprint on you. And of course you feel it now — in the silence, in the absence, in the spaces they used to fill. But pain has a way of romanticizing what hurt you, making you forget why you had to walk away in the first place. 

You didn’t leave without a reason. You didn’t choose distance without knowing something wasn’t right for you. And that truth doesn’t disappear just because you’re lonely, just because healing feels heavier than staying ever did. You can miss them and still know they are not where you belong. 

So if you’re thinking about going back, read this again. Let yourself feel it, but don’t let it lead you somewhere that already broke you. It’s okay to miss them. It’s okay to wish it had worked. But it’s also okay — and necessary — to keep choosing yourself anyway. 🖤

A page from the book ‘Daring To Take Up Space’ by 
Daniell Koepke 📖

caption.text:
The strange thing about being alive is how quickly it starts to feel normal.

You wake up inside a body you didn’t build, answer to a name someone gave you, carry a face you’ve never seen directly, and move through a world full of people having lives as private and complicated as your own.

At first, facts like these feel like little glitches in reality. Interesting, unsettling, almost funny. The kind of thing you read and then immediately want to tell someone else.

But the deeper point is not that life is strange.

The deeper point is that we stop noticing.

The brain is built to turn miracles into background noise. It has to. If you were constantly aware of how improbable and temporary everything is, you’d never get anything done. You’d just stand in the kitchen staring at your hands.

So the mind simplifies. It makes the moon ordinary. It makes your body ordinary. It makes time ordinary. It makes other people ordinary. It makes today feel like just another day.

Then one small fact breaks through and reminds you where you actually are.

On a planet.
In a body.
Inside time.
Surrounded by strangers who are also entire worlds.
Made out of matter older than memory.
Living a life that will someday feel impossible to explain.

caption.text:
You can be kind. You can be patient. You can do everything “right” — and still feel like you don’t belong.

caption.text:
Claiming the life you want 🖤 Start by getting crystal clear on what you truly want. Map it out in detail. Script a scene from your dream life—where you are, what you’re doing, who you’re with, how it feels. Make it vivid, specific, and real. (If you’re more visual, create a vision board—physical or digital. Whatever keeps the vision alive in your daily life.)

The important part is to see it and feel it every day. Let the emotions of living that life—joy, peace, excitement—become so familiar that it starts to feel inevitable.

Then affirm it to yourself: “I deserve this.” And don’t just say the words—believe them. Let them challenge every outdated belief that ever told you otherwise.

Because the moment you believe you deserve more, you’ll stop settling for less. You’ll stop chasing what doesn’t align. You’ll move differently, choose differently, and show up as someone who is already living the life they once only dreamed of.

— Words from the book ‘Detached’ by Sabrina Bendory 📖

The hardest thing you will have to do in life is to let go of the people you may want to hold onto. Sometimes, you will have to settle for loving someone from a distance, and that is okay. caption.text:
Sometimes the hardest thing to believe is that what’s meant for you doesn’t require you to chase it. That you don’t have to prove your worth, overextend your heart, or hold onto something that keeps slipping through your hands. But what is real, what is rooted, will meet you in peace — not in confusion, not in pressure. 

We spend so much time questioning why things didn’t work, why doors closed, why something we wanted so badly didn’t stay. But not everything that leaves is a loss. Some things leave because they were never meant to remain — they were only there to teach you, shape you, or redirect you. 

Even when it feels quiet, even when nothing seems to be happening, life is still moving things into place. The right people, the right timing, the right opportunities — they are finding their way to you in ways you cannot always see yet. 

You are not being overlooked. You are being prepared. So keep your heart open, even when it’s hard. What is meant for you will not pass you by — it will find you, and when it does, it will feel like peace. 🖤

📚 Read more in the book ‘Stay Single’ by Rebecca Simon

caption.text:
Absolutely nothing prepares you for losing a parent. It’s possibly the most important shift and transition you’ll ever experience in this life. 

The hardest moments are the days that follow, when the world you’ve spent your whole life building suddenly shatters. Everything disappears, and you realise that the only things left to hold onto are the sentimentals. 

Small things, like a piece of their clothing, or their favourite mug in the kitchen. Just their scent alone has the power to resurface so many feelings!

If you’re currently preparing to lose a parent, my advice is this: record everything. Capture the moments. Record their laugh, their stories, their voice. Ask them to create messages for your future milestones. Make sure that even if they’re no longer physically present, they’ve left behind something that gives you something to look forward to. One day, those small videos will mean everything.

This is for anyone who is grieving, or watching someone they love slip away.

💔 Preserve the love. It’s what keeps you going.
.
.
Clip taken from my recent conversation with @jayshetty on the On Purpose Podcast — Thanking @jayshetty for creating a space where I can freely talk about grief and the process of regaining a life afterwards. Check out the full episode on YouTube 🌻

caption.text:
There comes a moment in your life when you stop explaining yourself. Not because you have nothing left to say, but because you finally understand that the right people will never need an explanation for your worth. 

Growth doesn’t always look like healing in soft, beautiful ways. Sometimes it looks like exhaustion. Like finally being tired enough to walk away from what you once tolerated. Tired of overgiving, overproving, and overextending yourself for people who only meet you halfway. And that kind of tired? It’s not weakness. It’s awakening. 

Because the moment you stop accepting less is the moment everything begins to realign. You create space for what is actually meant for you—not what you begged for, not what you tried to fix, but what arrives naturally, peacefully, and fully. 

And maybe you don’t see it yet. Maybe it hasn’t arrived. But becoming the version of you who knows her worth will always come before receiving what she deserves. And once you reach that point… everything changes.

caption.text:
Sometimes we don’t let go because we’re weak. We don’t let go because we invested time, hope, love, identity. We convince ourselves that if we try harder, hold tighter, stay longer — we can save it. But not everything is meant to be saved.

When something is already ending, forcing it to stay only drains you. A relationship that has run its course. A version of you that you’ve outgrown. A dream that no longer fits. The hardest truth is this: what is dying in your life is not asking to be revived — it’s asking to be released.

Letting go is not failure. It is alignment. It is choosing your peace over your fear of starting over. It is trusting that what falls away is creating space for something stronger, healthier, more true.

caption.text:
I smile; because I still have the ability to do so. Recently, life has transformed itself into a traumatic accumulation of losses and a magnitude of change. Since October 2020; 15 members of my soul community, including both of my parents, Wale’s Father and 3 Friends all transitioned into the spiritual realm, leaving me behind to adult without the adults who raised me. The hardest and most significant departure was my darling Mother, who passed away in March 2021 from Cancer.
—
I smile; because I still have the ability to do so, but mostly because I made it. They thought I would die without my Mother but instead I developed more love and resilience. I endured a lot of abuse in my childhood from family, which trickled its way into adulthood, resulting in my behaviours and habits being deep-rooted in unhealthy coping mechanisms and trauma. I’m no longer honouring their secrets or carrying their shame. 
—
I was blessed and fortunate enough to have unconditional love for 31 years of my life from my Mother, but ever since she transitioned into the spiritual realm, I was abruptly made aware of how cold this world truly is. Which made the reasons behind why I started this platform more meaningful and intentional. I wanted to create a space online for everyone to experience the beauty of being poured into — with words of encouragement and love; an essence similar to my upbringing. I wanted to create a safe space. Community. Now that’s accomplished, I’m moving towards a higher vision, where I’ll be using my platforms to find healing resources for those with similar experiences, documenting my journey as I return home to myself and relaunching our Publishing House “The Good Publishing” connecting with writers who share a similar message. 

This is how you actively break generational curses. 
—
I Give Thanks to absolutely everyone who nurtured me during this time. Thank you for your patience. INFINITE INFINITE INFINITE LOVE. Thank You. All praise to the Most High. ❤️

caption.text:
Sometimes the hardest truth to accept is that not everyone is meant to recognize the depth of your heart. You can love deeply, show up fully, and still be met with someone who simply isn’t capable of holding what you offer. That doesn’t mean your love was too much — it means it was meant for someone else. 

Rejection often feels personal, but sometimes it is simply redirection. A quiet protection guiding you away from the places where your heart would have gone unseen, unheard, or unappreciated. Not every closed door is a loss. Some are mercy. 

The right love will not make you question your worth. It will meet your depth with depth, your softness with care, and your devotion with the same steady intention. The kind of love meant for you will recognize your heart immediately — and hold it with gentleness. 🖤

If this spoke to you read more in the book ‘Let Go, Trust God’ by Rebecca Simon 📖

caption.text:
The right love will never make you feel like you have to earn your place in someone’s life. It will not disappear the moment you become difficult to understand. It will not grow cold when you are hurting. The right person will sit beside your sadness without trying to escape it.

Because real love is not just found in the beautiful moments. It is found in the quiet ones too — the long conversations at midnight, the patience during your overthinking, the reassurance when your mind gets heavy, the way they continue choosing you even when life is not easy.

And maybe that is what makes love feel safe in the end. Not the grand gestures. Not the perfect timing. But the simple, steady presence of someone who stays gentle with your heart no matter what season of life you are in.

Find the one who makes love feel like peace. The one who stays.

caption.text:
Today, we are honored to debut The Lost Horses: Anthem Film set to Billie Eilish’s Oscar-winning song “What Was I Made For?”

It tells the story of horses who served us, trusted us — and were forgotten.

Every year, tens of thousands of horses — Thoroughbreds, ex–show jumpers, discarded lesson ponies, wild horses, and even donkeys — are lost to the darkness of the export pipeline.

They are companions.  Athletes.  Therapy partners.
Lives who gave everything, only to be thrown away.

And in their final moments, one haunting question lingers: 
What was I made for?

This powerful song carries that truth forward.  Horses have been our partners for centuries — and no life deserves to be discarded.

Thank you, Billie, for sharing your compassion, grace, and artistry with The Lost Horses.  Storytelling combined with advocacy has the extraordinary power to make lasting change in our world.

If this moved you, we ask you to join us in this movement.  Raise your voice, share this film, and take action —
so no horse is ever lost again.

www.losthorses.org

caption.text:
IMPORTANT NEWS.  An immediate halt on equine exports to Mexico due to the New World screwworm situation has been issued by APHIS.

The suspension includes horses exported for slaughter, breeding, work, sport, exhibition, and transit purposes.

While the duration of this measure remains unknown, it means that horses cannot currently be exported from the United States to Mexico through these channels. APHIS has not yet provided a timetable for resumption.

WBF will share updates as additional information becomes available.

As The Wild Beauty Foundation continues to fight for passage of the SAFE Act, including helping advance core protections through the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee alongside our partners, this development underscores an important reality: the horse slaughter pipeline can be stopped, should be stopped, and must be stopped.

Thank you for being part of this journey, and for standing with The Lost Horses.

#TheLostHorses #WildBeautyFoundation #SAFEAct

Hope.

Please watch, share, and help us shine a light, so we can make change together.  Take two minutes of your time and lend your voice by taking action at losthorses.org

It’s trying to protect you from disappointment. It’s trying to make sure you don’t make mistakes. But you don’t have to listen to every scary thought it throws at you.

You don’t need to figure out your whole future right now. You don’t need to know exactly how everything is going to work out before you allow yourself to relax.

You’ve gotten through a lot of things you didn’t know how to handle until you were actually in them. And somehow, each time, you figured it out.

I know it’s hard to trust that sometimes. I know uncertainty can make everything feel urgent. But not everything that feels urgent actually is.

You’re allowed to put some questions down for now.

The answers don’t always arrive when you’re searching for them. Sometimes they show up while you’re busy living your life.

And I hope you remember this:

You have never needed to have everything figured out to keep moving forward.

You’ve always been allowed to learn as you go.

caption.text:
There are seasons in life where simply continuing is an act of courage. Days where getting out of bed, answering messages, showing up to work, or just breathing through the heaviness feels like more than anyone around you realizes. Grief does not only live in the moments we lose someone — it lives in the quiet spaces afterward, in the ways life continues when your heart still feels paused. 

So if you are carrying something heavy right now — a loss, a heartbreak, a disappointment, a chapter you never expected to live through — please know that surviving it is already something to be proud of. You may feel like you are barely holding it together, but even that is a form of strength. Healing does not always look graceful. Sometimes it just looks like making it through the day. 

Grief asks you to walk through things you never should have had to face. And yet here you are, still moving forward in whatever way you can. That deserves gentleness. That deserves compassion. That deserves recognition. 

— Words from the book ‘If You’re Grieving’ by Jacqueline Whitney 🖤📖 @jacquelinewhitney_

caption.text:
The kind of love that stays, the kind that mirrors God’s love—it will not confuse you. It will not ask for you to water yourself down. It will not make you feel like you have to compete with an idealized version of yourself. Real love, holy love, shows up in your life with clarity. It shows up with presence. It shows up with willingness. It will choose you in the light, not just when it is convenient and full of virtue, but when it is dark all over, when it aches. Real love roots. It endures. 

If a human being failed to offer you that, no matter how much you hoped they would—they are not your destiny. They may have been a beautiful part of your becoming, but that does not mean that they were meant to stay. Some connections mark chapters in our lives, but they do not define the book itself. That doesn’t make the story any less valuable, any less tender; it just means that you can turn the page, it just means that you can trust that you have something special still ahead.

🖤 Continue reading in the book ‘Stay Single’ by Rebecca Simon.

caption.text:
I hope you believe that you can still make a beautiful life for yourself even if you lost many years of it to grief, or darkness, or a wound that wouldn’t close. I understand what it is like to have this world introduce you to your own shadow, to let the ache follow you around long after you have healed, convincing you that you aren’t worthy or capable of holding peace within yourself.

And so, if you have forgotten — I hope you know that the things that have battle-scarred you do not disqualify you from being able to experience something deep, and rooted, and tender in your lifetime.

If you have forgotten, I hope you know that you are worthy of the kind of love that shines warmth into all corners of you. You always have been.

Because at the end of the day, the most formidable thing about the right kind of love is that it will not just choose you in all that is light filled and perfect in your world. It will crack you open, it will find the rooms within your heart and your mind that are padlocked and hard to touch, and it will hold you there. It will understand you, and see you, and it will not run from you when the wound is scratched. It will stand firmly in front of you and hold your face between its palms and it will say, “It is okay to be who you are with me.”

The right kind of love will never judge you for who you had to be in order to navigate your sadness, in order to cut the ache from the bone. It will never fault you for the things you went through that you did not deserve, for the ways in which you were weathered by the people you placed your hope within. It wasn’t your fault. It wasn’t your fault.

Remember - your past does not prohibit you from the goodness that is trying to reach you. It does not make you ineligible, or undeserving of love, or connection, or the things you desire. You have the capacity to experience beauty, to nurture it within yourself, and when you are ready to move towards it, know that it will meet you where you are. Know that you have every right to hold it.

— Words by Bianca Sparacino 🖤
Read more in her book ‘The Strength In Our Scars’ 📖

caption.text:
Brumbies are being shot from the air. Listen to a live interview here in Australia with @ashleyavis.

We are on the ground in Sydney to document the aerial cull of thousands of iconic brumbies.

These wild horses, which live in and around Kosciuszko National Park, are being shot from helicopters in an operation ordered by the New South Wales government.

The cull has ignited intense debate across Australia and around the world, with many questioning the population estimates being used to justify the killing of one of Australia’s most iconic animals.

“This isn’t humane management,” says Avis. “If we want to talk about humane management, let’s sit down at the table to do that. But this issue, what’s happening with the culling - which is a very convenient and gentle word for killing - this is wrong, this is black and white, let’s come together to stop this.”

For detailed updates on this issue, follow @brumby_strong, and reach out to those in power by calling and tagging:

Penny Sharpe @pennysharpemlc
Chris Minns @chrisminnsmp
National Parks NSW @nswnationalparks
Anthony Albanese @albomp

As Avis concludes, “Penny Sharpe is the New South Wales Minister for Environment and Heritage… how an individual with such a title could order the violent massacre of brumbies who are part of Australia’s heritage is, in a word, shocking.”

caption.text:
You will realize that at some point—perhaps during a long lapse of attention—your life has become only your own again. Your triumphs and failures belong to you in a way that is enticing, invigorating, and just the slightest bit sad all at once. But it doesn’t make you want to run back to the past. You have grown comfortable in your autonomy, and it’s somewhere you kind of want to stay.

You’ll get over your ex when you meet someone new. Not when you hook up or shack up or even fall in love with another human being, but the first time you find yourself sitting across a crowded café table from someone whose smile melts you and whose arms you’d fit perfectly into, and yet some part of you is holding back. You’ll realize at that moment that life has ceased to be a frantic dash to find someone who can replace your ex or fill the aching hole they left inside of you. You’re putting your heart back together, and you want to do it properly before you jump feet-first into something new. You know that someday you will love someone else—that the capacity for affection and belonging is not lost on you and that you’re not going to end up alone. You’re not broken or hopeless or loveless just because your heart is aching—you are simply healing yourself. And when you’re done, there will be a whole new world waiting for you.

You will not get over your ex all at once. You’ll get over them through a series of tiny, tender moments that bring you quietly back to yourself. And in some ways, they’ll never really leave you. The people who change us in those big, irrevocable ways never do. To get over them, we’d have to alter ourselves into people so unrecognizable that we’d lose who we are in the process. And so instead, we learn to integrate the influence they had—the books you now read because of topics that they turned you on to. The music you now download because of the lyrics they loved. The ways you now look at the world that would never have occurred to you if they had not opened your eyes up to seeing and doing things differently.

📖 Continue reading in the book ‘This Is Me Letting You Go’ by Heidi Priebe

caption.text:
Sometimes the season you are in is not random — it is revealing. It is showing you what you need to let go of, what you need to trust, and what you are finally ready to grow into. The timing of your life is not something working against you, even when it feels like it is. It is often quietly working for you, aligning you with the lessons you are meant to learn right now. 

There are moments when things fall apart, when plans don’t work out, when you feel like you are being redirected without understanding why. But not everything that leaves your life is a loss. Some things are a release. Some things are protection. Some things are making space for something that is more aligned with who you are becoming. 

Growth does not always feel like progress. Sometimes it feels like uncertainty, like starting over, like questioning everything you once believed was meant for you. But even then, something within you is shifting. You are learning to trust what stays, to release what doesn’t, and to believe that what is meant for you will find you without force. 

No matter the chapter you are in, you are not behind. You are not lost. You are being guided into the version of your life that is actually meant for you — one step, one lesson, one moment at a time. 

— Pages from the book ‘The Pivot Year’ by Brianna Wiest 🖤📖

caption.text:
Sometimes the sign you are asking for isn’t a new person. Sometimes the sign is the peace you feel when you finally stop chasing what was never meant to stay. The right love will never require you to abandon yourself in order to keep it. It won’t ask you to become smaller, quieter, less emotional, less ambitious, or less you. The right love won’t feel like a puzzle you have to solve every day. It will feel like a safe place to rest.

Until then, keep building a life you are proud to wake up to. Keep choosing your healing. Keep choosing your growth. Keep becoming the person you were always meant to be. Love is not something you have to earn through suffering. It is something that meets you when you no longer believe you must sacrifice yourself to receive it.

And maybe that’s the reminder today: never settle for a connection that costs you your peace. The love meant for you will never make you question your worth. It will remind you of it.

Words inspired by the book ‘Stay Single’ by Rebecca Simon — a beautiful reminder that the healthiest love is never rushed, forced, or chased. It arrives when you are no longer willing to trade your peace for potential.

caption.text:
Another carriage horse has died in Central Park.

His name was Deniz.  According to NYPD officials, he was sixteen years old and was pulling a carriage carrying two passengers when he collapsed.

Officers who spoke with the driver reported that the horse appeared to suffer a medical emergency.

The cause of Deniz’s death remains unknown pending a necropsy, and authorities have stated there is no indication of criminality at this time.

While horses commonly live well into their twenties, and many reach their late twenties or even thirties, Deniz died at sixteen years old on the streets of Manhattan while working as a carriage horse.

Every horse deserves our respect and compassion.  Horses are athletes, companions, working animals, and trusted partners.

While the circumstances surrounding Deniz’s death have not yet been determined, his passing once again raises important questions about the continued use of horse-drawn carriages in one of the busiest and most congested urban environments in the world.

The Wild Beauty Foundation stands with advocates supporting Ryder’s Law and efforts to end the horse-drawn carriage industry in New York City.

We believe there is a difference between honoring history and preserving practices that may no longer reflect modern standards of equine welfare.

Today, our thoughts are with Deniz, and every horse who has died on the streets of New York.

#ryderslaw #carriagehorses #endhorsedrawncarriages

caption.text:
You are not powerful enough to ruin what is truly meant for you. Read that again. So many of us spend our lives worrying that we missed our chance, made the wrong decision, waited too long, started too late, or somehow stepped outside of the life we were supposed to have. What if the doors that belong in your life are not so fragile that they can be closed by one wrong turn? What if the things heaven has written into your story are still finding their way to you, even when you cannot see them?

There is so much peace in realizing that you do not have to chase every blessing down. You do not have to force timelines. You do not have to exhaust yourself trying to control what was never yours to control. Sometimes faith looks like releasing your grip and trusting that what is meant for you will arrive at the right time, in the right way.

This beautiful passage is from the book ‘Finding God Every Day’ by Rebecca Simon — a devotional for anyone who feels anxious about the future, struggles with trusting God’s timing, or needs a gentle reminder that they cannot miss what heaven has already set in motion for them. 🖤

caption.text:
And the truth is—once you have experienced peace, chaos will feel like a threat. It will not be something you run towards any longer; it will not be something you strive to keep. Once you have built a home within yourself, you stop accepting visitors who treat it without intention, and without tenderness. You stop letting inconsistency trick you into believing you have found connection. You stop mistaking intensity for intimacy. Because you’ve felt what it is like to be seen by God—to be loved in the quiet, to be held in the waiting, to be understood without performing, and after that, the almosts lose their magic. They fade in the light of what is real.

One day, love will find you again, but it will not look like the love that came before it. It will not arrive in your life with the intention of completing you—it will arrive with the intention of complementing what God has already completed within you. It will meet you in your peace, not your longing. It will recognize the life you have built on your own, and it will want to be a constructive part of it. It will be gentle. It will be intuitive. It will be clear. It will remind you that love was never supposed to be anchored to an almost—it was always meant to be about alignment.

Until then, keep choosing yourself.

— Get a copy of this book on Amazon ‘Stay Single’ by Rebecca Simon 🖤📖

caption.text:

caption.text:
When you are with the right person, time falls away. You don’t worry about fitting them into your complicated schedule because they become a part of that schedule. They become the backbone of it. Your happiness becomes your priority, and so long as they are contributing to it, you can work around the rest.

The right people don’t stand in the way of the things you once wanted and make you choose them over those things. The right people encourage you to try harder, dream bigger, and do better. They bring out the most incredible parts of yourself and make you want to fight harder than ever before. The right people don’t impose limits on your time, your dreams, or your abilities. They want to tackle those mountains with you, and they don’t care how long it takes. With the right person, you have all the time in the world.

The truth is, when we pass someone up because the timing is wrong, what we are really saying is that we don’t care to spend our time on that person. There will never be a magical time when everything falls into place and fixes all our broken relationships. But there may someday be a person who makes the issue of timing irrelevant.

Because when someone is right for us, we make the time to let them into our lives. And that kind of timing is always right.

📖 Book: This Is Me Letting You Go by Heidi Priebe (find your copy by following the link in our bio 🖤)

caption.text:
Sometimes the people who hurt us the most didn’t feel wrong in the beginning. They felt familiar. They felt exciting. They felt like chemistry. But often what we call “chemistry” is simply our nervous system recognizing patterns it learned long before we understood what love was supposed to feel like. When inconsistency, emotional distance, or chaos were once part of what we experienced as connection, our bodies can begin to mistake those things for passion. And so the wrong person can feel right — not because they are good for us, but because they are recognizable. 

Healing begins when we start questioning those patterns. When we realize that love was never meant to feel like anxiety, confusion, or constant uncertainty. Real love is steady. It is calm. It is consistent. And sometimes, when we are used to chaos, that calm can feel unfamiliar at first. But unfamiliar does not mean wrong — it often means healthy. 

Learning to choose differently requires retraining your nervous system, rewriting the story of what love should look like, and allowing yourself to believe that you deserve something softer, safer, and more secure than what you once accepted. The right person will not feel like a rollercoaster. They will feel like peace. 

📖 This reflection was inspired by the book ‘Detached’ by Sabrina Bendory, a powerful exploration of emotional patterns, healing, and learning to recognize the difference between familiarity and real love. 🖤

caption.text:
How to move on after losing your mother? Find something new to pour your love into. 
. 
That was the advice I received from my godmother. At the time, it felt impossible. But over the past 4years, I’ve been trying my best to find things to love, until I realised the first thing I needed to focus on was myself. 
.
Grief absolutely crippled me but being faced with the reality of how ugly family can be, really highlighted how much my mother protected me.
. 
I realised that I spent a whole lifetime breaking my own heart due to the ricochet of the treatment I received growing up which resulted in me treating myself the same way. I wanted to stop that pattern. I wanted to break those chains. So I decided to do the one thing they always told me not to do: share my story. 
.
I decided to put everything into a book and build a community of people who went through the same thing, to speak to them and let them know that even though people around you may have spent years trying to break your heart, and even though you may have normalised that behaviour and ended up breaking your own heart, you can still return home to yourself. 
.
Because there is a beautiful life out there, a life that needs to be lived, that you have a right to pursue. And the quicker you fix your broken heart, the quicker you get to enjoy this human experience.
.
I learned a lot about forgiveness. I learned how to filter my community. I learned how to walk away from people I never thought I would have to walk away from and still have peace in my heart. I learned how to handle my pain.
.
I learned how to love myself again and how much it takes. The routines, the new habits, the lifestyle changes, everything you have to rebuild when you lose your rock.
.
So, if anyone reading this has lost a parent, pour your love into something else. The love your parent(s) left behind for you has manifested into a seed. You need to bury it, take care of it, and allow that seed to grow. That’s how you keep them alive. 
.
My mother always used to say, “People only die when you stop talking about them” and 65k have read her name.
.
Thank you to everyone who brought a copy of my book and made this possible. 🌻

caption.text:
There’s a specific kind of heartbreak that doesn’t come from losing someone — it comes from slowly losing yourself while trying to keep them.

You don’t notice it at first. You just start shrinking in small ways. Saying less. Wanting less. Needing less. You call it compromise, patience, understanding… but really, you’re editing your personality so you’re easier to love. You start becoming a softer version of yourself, not because you’ve grown — but because you’re afraid that being fully you is “too much.”

And the painful part? Even after all that bending, they still don’t meet you where you are. You change… and they stay the same. You move backward trying to hold on, while the relationship keeps asking you to disappear just a little bit more.

Love isn’t supposed to cost you your identity. It’s not meant to make you question your worth, dim your personality, or feel like you have to earn basic care. The right love doesn’t ask you to become smaller — it gives you space to expand. It feels warm. Safe. Like you can exhale and still be chosen.

Sometimes walking away isn’t giving up on love — it’s choosing yourself so you don’t have to abandon who you are just to be loved.

📖 ‘Beauty In The Stillness’ by Karin Hadadan (find it by following the link in our bio)

caption.text:
Grief doesn’t just take something from you — it reshapes you. It teaches you what it means to hold love with nowhere to place it, to carry memories that no longer have a home in the present. 

It’s not just missing them. It’s the quiet moments that follow — the instinct to reach for them, the way their absence shows up in the smallest parts of your day. It’s learning how to exist in a world that kept moving when something inside of you paused. 

And maybe the hardest part isn’t only that they’re gone, but that it changes how you trust, how you open up, how you let people in again. You wonder if your heart will ever feel safe the same way it once did. 

But grief is also proof that you loved deeply. That something real existed. And even if you carry it with you forever, it doesn’t mean you won’t find your way back to warmth, to connection, to feeling whole again — in a different way, but still whole. 🖤

Read more in the book ‘Altar’ by Tori Gordon 📖

caption.text:
And nothing has ever been the same since. 🥲

Life has changed in so many ways. Things have gotten complicated and life can be a lot at times.

We’re not kids anymore. This is the real world. There are no more all knowing adults to take care of everything for us, or tell us everything will be okay.

It’s up to us now to decide how we live our lives and where we end up. It’s a lot of responsibility none of us asked for, but here we are.

It can be overwhelming. Trust me, I feel all the same pressure as you, I get it.

But one thing I’ve learned is that no matter how hard things get or how complicated life becomes we always adapt.

We’re stronger and more capable than we realize.

If you’re reading this, you’ve overcome every single challenge so far. You’re still here, still breathing, still pushing forward.

You should be proud of yourself. It hasn’t been easy. And the hard truth is that it doesn’t get easier.

You just become stronger. More resilient. More wise.

You’re going to continue to grow and evolve. You’re going to realize that no matter what life throws at you, you will be okay.

Our parents might not be telling us that anymore but that’s okay, because we’re learning how to tell it to ourselves, and actually believe it.

I believe in you, because I believe in me. We’re all gonna make it. We’re all gonna be okay. 

We got this ❤️

Words by, @thehunterfogarty

caption.text:
We call it growth when it’s really disconnection. We call it love when it’s really fear—fear of being alone, fear of wasted time, fear that this is the best version of love we will get to experience.

But God loves you too much to let you stay in a place where you have to quiet your heart. And so, when you didn’t have the words to ask for better—he answered anyway. When you were too afraid to let go, He closed the door for you.

Some goodbyes feel like heartbreak when they are really just a form of guidance. Some endings feel like rejection when they are really just a form of alignment. Some human beings walk away, not because you weren’t valuable or worthy of tenderness, but because your spirit was outgrowing what they were never willing to expand within. Even though it didn’t look like grace at the time, it was. It was the break you needed to finally be set free. It was the unanswered prayer that saved you from settling for less than what you were created for.

Because the truth is—you were never meant to endure what continually wounds you. You were never meant to feel like love is something you have to settle for or earn through suffering.

📖 Continue reading in the book ‘Stay Single’ by Rebecca Simon (available on Amazon).

caption.text:
Marlon Brando was one of the most influential figures in film history — an actor who transformed Hollywood with a style of performance that felt raw, authentic, and deeply human.

Born in Omaha, Nebraska, in 1924, he grew up in a troubled household marked by instability and emotional hardship. Far removed from the fame that would later define him, Brando spent his early years searching for purpose and belonging.

Through determination and natural talent, he rose to prominence in the 1950s and became one of the most celebrated actors of his generation. His performances in films such as A Streetcar Named Desire, On the Waterfront, and The Godfather redefined screen acting, bringing an unprecedented level of realism and emotional depth to the cinema.

What made Brando different was the complexity behind the legend. He possessed immense charisma and commanded attention wherever he went, yet he often felt uneasy with fame and resisted many of Hollywood’s expectations. 

Behind the public image was a thoughtful and often conflicted man who cared deeply about social justice and used his influence to support causes he believed in.

Throughout his life, Brando experienced extraordinary success as well as profound personal struggles. He became the father of eleven children and endured both great joys and heartbreaking losses. The contradictions that shaped his life also contributed to the depth and vulnerability audiences saw in his work.

He died on July 1, 2004, at the age of 80, but his influence has never faded. Marlon Brando remains a symbol of cinematic excellence — not just because he was a great star, but because he changed the very language of acting.

Even today, his legacy can be found in countless performances inspired by his example: the courage to strip away artifice and reveal something truthful beneath.

#marlonbrando #oldhollywood #vintageaesthetics #vintageglamour

caption.text:
Hedy Lamarr was one of the most fascinating figures of 20th-century Hollywood. Behind the glamour and elegance was a brilliant and inventive mind that longed to be recognized for more than her appearance.

Born as Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler in Vienna, Austria, in 1914, she was curious, intelligent, and fascinated by how things worked. Hollywood transformed her into Hedy Lamarr, one of the biggest stars of her era, but she hoped people would see beyond her beauty.

While acting in successful films, she helped develop a frequency-hopping communication system during World War II, an invention that later contributed to technologies such as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Yet for many years, her scientific achievements received little attention.

Her personal life was often turbulent. She was married six times and had three children, but despite her fame and many relationships, she often struggled to find lasting happiness and understanding.

As she grew older, Lamarr withdrew from public life and lived much of her later years in privacy. When she died in 2000 at the age of 85, she left behind more than a legendary film career. She became a lasting symbol of beauty, intelligence, and the remarkable achievements that can exist behind a famous face.

#hedylamarr #oldhollywood #goldenageofhollywood #silverscreenstar #vintageglamour
